status.green.title: All clear

status.amber.body: Some items need a look. No critical cyber incident is open.

panel.activity.hint: Bars show switch approvals. Red dots mark hours with new alerts.
how.watch.body: Reads copies of the switch, ledger and settlement logs. Never sits in the payment path.
how.match.body: Every approval must meet its ledger posting within {window} seconds.
how.mask.body: Aadhaar, PAN, card and account numbers are masked before anything is stored.
how.report.body: A confirmed alert becomes a pre-filled DAKSH / CERT-In report with a 6-hour clock.
network.offline.hint: Detection continues on this computer. Messages are queued and sent when the line returns.
rule.SG-R1.name: Approval without ledger debit
rule.SG-R1.message: The switch approved {amount} (RRN {rrn}, {channel}) but no matching debit reached the core-banking ledger within {window} seconds. Money may have left the bank without any customer account being debited.
rule.SG-R2.name: Credit without funding
rule.SG-R2.message: {amount} was credited to account {account} (RRN {rrn}) although the network transaction failed or was reversed. The remitter was not debited.
rule.SG-R3.name: Duplicate or replayed transaction
rule.SG-R3.message: The same transaction (RRN {rrn}) was processed {count} times in the {feed_name}. This can be a replayed or duplicated message.
rule.SG-R4.name: Amount mismatch
rule.SG-R4.message: Switch and ledger disagree on RRN {rrn}: switch {switch_amount}, ledger {ledger_amount} (difference {amount}).
rule.SG-R5.name: Abnormal burst
rule.SG-R5.account.message: Account {account} had {window_count} {direction_word} approvals within {window_min} minutes ({episode_count} so far in this burst).
rule.SG-R5.foreign.message: {window_count} withdrawals at foreign terminals in {countries} countries within {window_min} minutes ({episode_count} so far). This matches card-cloning cash-out attacks.
rule.SG-R6.name: Settled by network, never approved by bank
rule.SG-R6.message: The payment network settled a debit of {amount} (RRN {rrn}) that this bank's switch never approved. Approvals may be coming from an unauthorised (proxy) switch.
rule.SG-R7.name: Ledger debit without approval
rule.SG-R7.message: The ledger debited {amount} from account {account} for RRN {rrn}, but the switch has no approval for it.
rule.SG-R8.name: Customer credit missing
rule.SG-R8.message: The network confirmed a credit of {amount} for account {account} (RRN {rrn}), but the account was not credited.
actions.UNAUTHORISED_DEBITS: Isolate the ATM/UPI switch from the payment network and inform your technology service provider and NPCI.
Block the affected cards and stop stand-in or offline approvals until the switch is verified.
Preserve switch logs and take a disk image of the switch server before any clean-up.
File the incident on DAKSH and notify CERT-In within 6 hours of detection.
actions.ERRONEOUS_CREDITS: Suspend the affected inward channel (IMPS/UPI) until the posting fault is fixed.
Mark a lien on beneficiary accounts that received unfunded credits to stop withdrawals.
Reconcile with the network settlement and start recovery.
File the incident on DAKSH and notify CERT-In within 6 hours of detection.
actions.INTEGRITY: Check the interface between the switch and core banking for tampering or faults.
Reverse duplicate or wrong postings only after verification.
Preserve interface logs and message queues.
If confirmed as a cyber incident, file on DAKSH and notify CERT-In within 6 hours.
actions.CUSTOMER_SERVICE: Credit the customer, or return the money to the remitter, within the RBI turnaround time.
Check the inward posting queue for stuck messages.
alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.intro: Each alert is a transaction or burst that did not reconcile. All evidence is masked.
incidents.title: Incidents
incidents.intro: Related alerts are grouped into incidents. Every reportable incident has a 6-hour reporting clock that starts at detection.
incident.not_reportable: Operational issue, not a cyber incident. Resolve within the RBI turnaround time.
timeline.NOTIFIED: Message queued for the branch manager
demo.title: Demo lab
demo.intro: Replays a synthetic day at a small co-operative bank and injects a known attack pattern. All data is synthetic.
demo.reset_confirm: Delete all alerts, incidents and runs?
scenario.normal.name: Normal day
scenario.normal.desc: Ordinary traffic with declines, reversals and late postings. Should raise no alerts.
scenario.cosmos.name: Proxy-switch cash-out
scenario.cosmos.desc: Cloned cards withdraw cash at foreign ATMs at night while a malicious switch approves them without debiting the ledger (2018 Cosmos Bank pattern).
scenario.uco.name: Credits without debits
scenario.uco.desc: Inward IMPS credits are posted even though the remitter's transaction was reversed, and a few accounts exploit it repeatedly (2023 UCO Bank IMPS pattern).
scenario.replay.name: Replayed messages
scenario.replay.desc: The same debit is posted twice in the core-banking ledger.
scenario.tamper.name: Amount tampering
scenario.tamper.desc: An interface changes the amount between the switch and the ledger.
scenario.ghost.name: Debits without approval
scenario.ghost.desc: Debits appear in the ledger with no switch approval (insider or interface fault).
scenario.missing.name: Missing customer credits
scenario.missing.desc: The network confirms inward credits that never reach the customer's account.
scenario.slowcbs.name: Core banking running slow
scenario.slowcbs.desc: No attack: ledger postings arrive 4 to 8 minutes late for 20 minutes. Alerts are raised, then close themselves when the postings arrive.
upload.title: Upload log files
upload.intro: Upload copies of the three feeds for one period. Files are processed on this computer; nothing is sent outside.
upload.need_files: Choose at least the switch log and the ledger.
privacy.title: Privacy shield
privacy.intro: Masks Aadhaar, PAN, card, mobile and account numbers, e-mail and UPI IDs. Reference numbers (RRN/UTR) stay visible for investigators.
privacy.csv.hint: Columns are recognised by name and unknown columns are scanned. Account and card columns also get a pseudonymous token so records can still be joined.

bench.intro: Each scenario is injected into a synthetic day of normal traffic and scored against the known answer.
bench.none: No benchmark yet. Run it to measure detection on synthetic data.
about.title: About Sahakari-Guard
about.p1: Most co-operative banks reconcile their payment switch with the core-banking ledger once a day. Large frauds have happened in that gap: approvals that never reached the ledger, and credits that were never funded.
about.p2: Sahakari-Guard reads copies of three logs and checks, transaction by transaction, that the switch, the ledger and the network agree. It masks personal data before storing anything and turns a confirmed problem into a draft report for the 6-hour deadline.
about.l1: Prototype tested on synthetic data only. A pilot with real (masked) logs is the next step.
about.l2: Each bank needs a small adapter that converts its switch and core-banking exports to the canonical CSV format.
about.l3: Reports are drafts for a human officer. They are not an official RBI format.
about.l4: Tamil and Hindi text should be reviewed by native speakers before a pilot.
report.title: Cyber-incident report
report.subtitle: Draft for officer review
report.notice: Generated by Sahakari-Guard from masked evidence. Verify every field before filing on the RBI DAKSH portal and notifying CERT-In. This is not an official RBI format.
report.filing.daksh: File the incident on DAKSH (https://daksh.rbi.org.in) within 6 hours of detection.
report.filing.preserve: Preserve original logs and system images. Do not clean up before evidence is copied.
report.filing.board: Inform the CISO and senior management as per the bank's cyber crisis management plan.
report.description: {count} suspicious transaction(s) were detected by {rules}. The amount at risk is {amount} across {accounts} customer account(s). The first suspicious transaction was at {first} and Sahakari-Guard raised the first alert at {detected}.
report.more_alerts: … and {n} more alerts (see the JSON export).
notify.title: Sahakari-Guard: {severity} incident {incident_id}
notify.body: {family}. {count} transaction(s), {amount} at risk. Report due by {deadline}.
